prompt.context: Our client is the private division of a retail bank that has 100,000 clients, $500,000,000 in revenues, and $150,000,000 in net income. Our client's goal is to double the revenues and profits of the business in 5 years.
prompt.question: Assess the feasibility of the goal. Prioritize the two or three most important steps they should take in their action plan.

clarifying_info.q: How does the bank generate revenues?
clarifying_info.a: They make revenues from interest and fees.

clarifying_info.q: What are the main cost drivers?
clarifying_info.a: Transaction costs and salaries. The nature of the sale is a one-on-one pitch between the bank salesperson and the customer, so salary costs and transaction costs tend to be high.

clarifying_info.q: What is the bank's geographic footprint?
clarifying_info.a: They have a large presence in the North East and a moderate presence in the South East.

clarifying_info.q: What products does the bank offer?
clarifying_info.a: They have 4 product lines. By revenue rank: 1) Private banking (deposits, loans), 2) Investment management (brokerage, advice, access), 3) Trust (estate planning and trust, transferred death), 4) Insurance. By profit rank: 1) Private banking, 2) Trust (tied with Insurance), 3) Investment management.

Customers are segmented into 5 groups by asset volume: Ultra High ($10M+, 5% of customers), High Net ($1M-$10M, 10%), Affluent ($0.5M-$1M, 20%), Mass Affluent ($100K-$500K, 25%), Mass ($0-$100K, 40%). The top 3 segments (Ultra High, High Net, Affluent) generate 60-70% of revenues; the bottom 2 generate 30-40%.

clarifying_info.q: How many products does the average customer buy?
clarifying_info.a: 20-25% of customers purchase more than one product. 75-80% of customers purchase only one product.

exhibits.title: Customer Segmentation by Volume and Number
exhibits.shows: A table listing the five customer segments with their asset volume ranges and share of total customer count.
exhibits.data: Ultra High: $10M+, 5% of customers; High Net: $1M-$10M, 10%; Affluent: $0.5M-$1M, 20%; Mass Affluent: $100,000-$500,000, 25%; Mass: $0-$100,000, 40%

framework: Understand current revenue and profit baseline ($500M revenue, $150M net income, 100K clients)
Identify revenue growth levers: new customers vs. existing customer expansion
Analyze customer mix: top 3 segments (Ultra High, High Net, Affluent) generate 60-70% of revenue but are only 35% of clients
Analyze product mix: 4 product lines; 75-80% of customers buy only one product — large cross-sell opportunity
Assess buyer selection strategy: shift mix toward higher-value segments
Quantify cross-sell opportunity to test feasibility of doubling revenue
Assess cost implications: transaction costs are similar across segments, favoring focus on higher-revenue customers
Synthesize into prioritized action plan with 2-3 steps

questions.prompt: Is it feasible to double revenues to $1B in 5 years through cross-selling alone?
questions.guidance: A strong answer focuses on the top 3 customer segments (35% of clients, 60-70% of revenue) and uses the 75% single-product stat to quantify upside from cross-sell. Candidate should recognize that if products are comparably sized in revenue, selling all 4 products to current single-product customers in top segments could more than double revenue.

math.setup: Focus on top 3 segments. Assume 70% of revenue comes from them. 75% of those customers have only 1 product. If 4 products generate comparable revenues, cross-selling the other 3 products to each single-product customer multiplies their revenue contribution by 4.
steps: Revenue from top-3-segment customers who have only one product = $350M x 75% = $262.5M
If we cross-sell each of those customers the other 3 products (total of 4 products per customer, revenues equal across products), new revenue from this group = $262.5M x 4 = $1,050M
Total potential revenue (cross-sell group $1,050M + remaining customers) exceeds $1B target
math.answer: Cross-selling existing top-3-segment customers from 1 product to all 4 products could generate ~$1,050M from that group alone, well above the $1B revenue target. Feasibility confirmed.

questions.prompt: Which customer segments should the bank prioritize, and why?
questions.guidance: Since transaction costs are roughly the same across segments but revenue per customer is far higher in the top 3 segments (Ultra High, High Net, Affluent), the bank should concentrate growth efforts there. The bottom 2 segments (Mass Affluent, Mass) are less profitable on a per-customer basis relative to the cost to serve.

brainstorming.prompt: What specific actions could the bank take to grow revenues and shift its customer mix toward higher-value segments?

categories.name: Cross-Sell to Existing Customers
ideas: Give sales force incentives (bonuses, commissions) tied to cross-sell metrics
Bundle products to make it easy for customers to add services
Use data analytics to identify which existing customers are likely candidates for each product
Assign dedicated relationship managers to top-3-segment clients

categories.name: Attract Higher-Value New Customers
ideas: Run targeted marketing campaigns aimed at Ultra High, High Net, and Affluent segments
Sponsor high-net-worth events and communities (wealth management seminars, charity galas)
Build referral programs incentivizing existing top clients to refer peers
Partner with family offices, accountants, or attorneys who serve HNW clients

categories.name: Manage Down Lower-Value Segments
ideas: Raise fees/minimum balance requirements for Mass and Mass Affluent to encourage them to move to lower-cost competitors
Reduce one-on-one sales effort for bottom segments; shift to digital/self-service
Redirect freed-up capacity toward higher-value customer acquisition and service

categories.name: Geography and Product Expansion
ideas: Expand into new geographies where HNW populations are growing (e.g., West Coast, Texas)
Grow underperforming product lines (Trust, Insurance) through specialist hiring or acquisition
Develop new products relevant to top-segment needs (alternative investments, estate planning)

categories.name: Operational Efficiency
ideas: Invest in technology to reduce transaction costs per client
Standardize back-office processes to create capacity for higher-value advisory work

recommendation: It is feasible to double revenues and profits in 5 years primarily through cross-selling existing top-segment customers to all four product lines
The math shows that cross-selling the 75% of top-3-segment customers who currently have only one product across all 4 products could generate over $1B in revenue, exceeding the target
risks: Cross-sell rates may be lower than assumed if products don't address the same customer needs
Firing bottom-2-segment customers reduces headcount and may have reputational risk
Expanding geographically requires upfront investment and time to build relationships
Incentive structures for sales force may be hard to design and could encourage mis-selling
next_steps: Implement sales force incentives tied to cross-sell KPIs across all four product lines
Launch selective marketing and promotions targeting Ultra High, High Net, and Affluent customer segments
Increase prices or minimum thresholds for Mass and Mass Affluent segments to improve margin mix and redirect resources
